scenes.tts: Does an axon read an address in its own receptor level, or its rank among the others?
scenes.visual: Title card: Two Maps from One Retina. Two labels: address, rank.
scenes.narration: Does an axon read an address in its own receptor level, or its rank among the others?

scenes.tts: In a normal animal, both readings put the axons in the same order. To tell them apart, change some axons but not their neighbours.
scenes.visual: Two ordered maps, labelled fixed threshold and pure rank: same order, slightly different spacing (middle axon at 0.25 in one, 0.5 in the other).
scenes.narration: In a normal animal, both readings put the axons in the same order. To tell them apart, change some axons but not their neighbours.

scenes.tts: In two thousand, Arthur Brown, Greg Lemke and colleagues built such a mouse.
scenes.caption: In 2000, Arthur Brown, Greg Lemke and colleagues built such a mouse.
scenes.visual: Label: Brown, Lemke and colleagues, 2000. A mouse; its target labelled superior colliculus (the mouse version of the tectum).
scenes.narration: In 2000, Arthur Brown, Greg Lemke and colleagues built such a mouse.

scenes.tts: Isle two is a gene switched on in about half of the retinal ganglion cells, scattered across the retina.
scenes.caption: Isl2 is a gene switched on in about half of the retinal ganglion cells, scattered across the retina.
scenes.visual: Retina drawn as an irregular, intermingled mosaic of glowing and unglowing ganglion cells, with some same-colour cells side by side; no strict alternation. Label: Isl2 cells, about half, scattered.
scenes.narration: Isl2 is a gene switched on in about half of the retinal ganglion cells, scattered across the retina.

scenes.tts: They inserted the receptor Eff A three into that gene. Mouse ganglion cells do not normally make it.
scenes.caption: They inserted the receptor EphA3 into that gene. Mouse ganglion cells do not normally make it.
scenes.visual: The EphA3 coding sequence slides into the Isl2 gene. Label: knock-in.
scenes.narration: They inserted the receptor EphA3 into that gene. Mouse ganglion cells do not normally make it.

scenes.tts: Now neighbours at every point in the retina differed.
scenes.caption: Now neighbours at every point in the retina differed.
scenes.visual: Glowing cells gain extra receptor bars; the unglowing cells intermingled with them keep normal bars.
scenes.narration: Now neighbours at every point in the retina differed.

scenes.tts: Use the toy numbers. The knock-in adds four units, so knock-in axons carry five to seven. Their unchanged neighbours carry one to three.
scenes.visual: Table on screen: rows knock-in axons (5 to 7 units) and unchanged neighbours (1 to 3 units); columns absolute (fixed threshold) and relative (pure rank); all cells show question marks.
scenes.narration: Use the toy numbers. The knock-in adds four units, so knock-in axons carry five to seven. Their unchanged neighbours carry one to three.

scenes.tts: First, the absolute reading, a fixed threshold. Where do the knock-in axons go, and their unchanged neighbours?
scenes.visual: The absolute column is highlighted. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: First, the absolute reading, a fixed threshold. Where do the knock-in axons go, and their unchanged neighbours?

scenes.tts: In the toy, the knock-in axons crowd toward the front. The unchanged axons keep exactly their normal places.
scenes.visual: Absolute column fills: knock-in, crowd at the front edge; unchanged, normal full map.
scenes.narration: In the toy, the knock-in axons crowd toward the front. The unchanged axons keep exactly their normal places.

scenes.tts: Now the relative reading, in its simplest form: pure rank. Where does each group go?
scenes.visual: The pure rank column is highlighted. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Now the relative reading, in its simplest form: pure rank. Where does each group go?

scenes.tts: Every knock-in axon outranks every unchanged one. So knock-in axons take the front half, and unchanged axons the back.
scenes.visual: Relative column fills: knock-in, ordered map in the front half; unchanged, ordered map in the back half.
scenes.narration: Every knock-in axon outranks every unchanged one. So knock-in axons take the front half, and unchanged axons the back.

scenes.tts: In mice with two copies of the knock-in, Brown and colleagues found two orderly maps.
scenes.visual: Traces in the superior colliculus (mouse target): glowing knock-in axons fill the front half; unchanged axons fill the back half.
scenes.narration: In mice with two copies of the knock-in, Brown and colleagues found two orderly maps.

scenes.tts: Look at the unchanged axons. Nothing about them was altered, yet they ended somewhere new.
scenes.visual: The unchanged axons are highlighted, with a ghost of their normal positions further forward.
scenes.narration: Look at the unchanged axons. Nothing about them was altered, yet they ended somewhere new.

scenes.tts: An absolute reading cannot produce that. Their place depended on the other axons.
scenes.visual: The fixed-threshold column dims; a check mark appears on the pure rank column.
scenes.narration: An absolute reading cannot produce that. Their place depended on the other axons.

scenes.tts: So is the amount of ligand irrelevant? Try a thought test. Lower the eff-rin A everywhere, say by half.
scenes.caption: So is the amount of ligand irrelevant? Try a thought test. Lower the ephrin-A everywhere, say by half.
scenes.visual: The ephrin-A slope on the target lightens to half its shade.
scenes.narration: So is the amount of ligand irrelevant? Try a thought test. Lower the ephrin-A everywhere, say by half.

scenes.tts: What does each reading predict now?
scenes.visual: Two columns again, fixed threshold and pure rank. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: What does each reading predict now?

scenes.tts: The fixed threshold says the map shifts back. Pure rank says nothing moves, because no rank has changed.
scenes.visual: Fixed threshold: the map slides toward the back. Pure rank: the map stays put. Label: toy predictions.
scenes.narration: The fixed threshold says the map shifts back. Pure rank says nothing moves, because no rank has changed.

scenes.tts: Real mice with one working copy of each of two eff-rin A genes kept a normal main zone.
scenes.caption: Real mice with one working copy of each of two ephrin-A genes kept a normal main zone.
scenes.visual: Label: example ephrin-A2 and ephrin-A5 double heterozygote. A dense termination zone sits at the wild-type position, with a small extra zone further back.
scenes.narration: Real mice with one working copy of each of two ephrin-A genes kept a normal main zone.

scenes.tts: But in some animals, temporal axons also formed an extra patch further back.
scenes.visual: The small posterior extra zone glows. Label: ectopic patch, some animals.
scenes.narration: But in some animals, temporal axons also formed an extra patch further back.

scenes.tts: Pure rank cannot give that. The amount of ligand affects how accurately axons map.
scenes.visual: Only the pure rank column dims. Label: ligand dosage affects mapping accuracy.
scenes.narration: Pure rank cannot give that. The amount of ligand affects how accurately axons map.

scenes.tts: So neither toy is the whole story. In mouse and chick, the slope sets the scale. Comparison among axons sets who goes where.
scenes.visual: Both toy columns fade to grey. On screen: the slope sets the scale; the comparison sets the order.
scenes.narration: So neither toy is the whole story. In mouse and chick, the slope sets the scale. Comparison among axons sets who goes where.

scenes.tts: Slopes help lay out the coarse map. Correlated activity in the retina helps sharpen it, partly at the same time. That is the next unit.
scenes.visual: Broad termination zones in the colliculus tighten into sharp spots while the ephrin-A slope stays visible behind them. Label: overlapping in time.
scenes.narration: Slopes help lay out the coarse map. Correlated activity in the retina helps sharpen it, partly at the same time. That is the next unit.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: an axon's place is a rank, set against a slope.
scenes.visual: On screen: a rank set against a slope.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: an axon's place is a rank, set against a slope.
